Hi Gina — thanks, and yep we can get that to you. Attaching a first-pass diagram and a one-page choreography summary; Marissa (security architecture) and Vanessa (runtime product) are looped in for the technical detail.

High-level summary:
- Trust boundaries: customer workloads run in their VPC (Private deployment) with a private control plane link back to a customer-managed bastion or customer-sidepoint; the control-plane signaling is strictly mutual-TLS with mTLS cert pinning to the customer's KMS-backed identity. Our optional hosted control-plane path uses customer-specific tenancy isolation with per-tenant service accounts and encrypted channeling via dedicated VPC peering.
- Egress & sidecar comms: the inference sidecar communicates to the GPU runtime over an intra-host Unix socket when colocated, or an encrypted service mesh connection (mTLS) inside the private subnets. Egress to external services (metrics, S3) is routed through a customer-configured egress gateway or optional Redwood-managed egress proxy when customers opt into managed telemetry. Egress is restricted by default and must be explicitly whitelisted.
- Fallback choreography (short): if Dedicated GPU pool capacity is saturated or an instance fails, requests are routed per-policy: 1) retry on alternative node in same pool within a short backoff window; 2) if pool-level retries fail, requests fall back to a pinned, quantized CPU-accelerated model variant in the customer's private deployment zone (same trust boundary); 3) when private variants are unavailable and customer allows hosted fallback, we route to a Redwood-hosted, tenant-isolated model variant with additional logging and shortened retention window. In all cases we annotate telemetry with reason codes (NODE_FAIL, POOL_SATURATION, POLICY_FALLBACK) for audit.

Gina — adding the requested threat-mitigation summary below (short form). See attached artifacts for mapping to diagram labels. Happy to expand any item into evidence (config screenshots, audit logs, packet filters).

Threats and mitigations (summary):
- Cross-tenant data exfiltration via shared runtime: mitigated by tenant-scoped process isolation, per-tenant KV cache namespaces, and enforced filesystem eviction policies. We run per-tenant inoculation tests during onboarding.
- Lateral movement from control plane -> runtime: control plane signaling uses short-lived, customer-bound mTLS certs, role-restricted service accounts, and mutual attestation using hardware-backed keys (HSM/KMS). We also provide token-scoped session timeouts and can disable control-plane-initiated model uploads if customers require a read-only model pin.
- Compromised sidecar leading to network egress: sidecars run with minimal capabilities, eBPF-based egress enforcement (iptables replacements) in Private deployments, and an optional external egress gateway with allowlist enforcement. We also provide checksum-signed model artifacts and a runtime integrity monitor that alerts on binary drift.
- Fallback model integrity risk: fallbacks use signed model bundles with provenance metadata. When routing to Redwood-hosted fallbacks, we enforce additional data redaction hooks and a separate short-retention index for logs.

Evidence we can provide on request: network ACL exports, sample audit-trace for a failed node fallback (anonymized), HSM attestation report template, and our model-signing key-policies.

Marissa Cole
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Gina — following up to confirm you received the artifacts and the short threat summary. Quick answers to two likely follow-ups you mentioned on the call:

1) Audit telemetry fields we emit when a fallback occurs: fallback_reason, original_request_id, routed_model_variant, origin_zone, timestamp, audit_source_ip (redacted per policy), and policy_decision_id. We can push these to your SIEM via secure webhook or SFTP drop.

2) Data residency during hosted fallback: when hosted fallback is enabled we restrict the fallback to the same region and apply a KMS-envelope that ensures logs and tokens for those requests are kept in a dedicated, short-retention bucket under your tenancy.
